subject: GreenStreet Health — private deployment keystore & operator access guardrails
messages:
From: Sarah Lowe <sarah.lowe@greenstreethealth.com>
To: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
Cc: alan.yeung@greenstreethealth.com, dpa-legal@heronlaw.com
Date: Mon, 2 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: GreenStreet — private deploy DPA + keystore questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are moving toward an internal security review for a private deployment (VPC/on-prem) and need to align on a few contract items before procurement can proceed:

- Customer-controlled keys (BYOK): can your private package support a customer-managed CMK such that Redwood has zero ability to decrypt customer payloads? We need language that establishes separation and no operator access to plaintext.
- Operator access & telemetry: what minimal telemetry/logs will Redwood retain for the private control plane? We need assurances around redaction, retention windows, and evidence for audit.
- Subprocessors: please provide a list of subprocessors that could access metadata for the private deployment and the proposed notification timeline for adding new subprocessors.
- Cross-border transfers: our legal team needs clear language about whether any customer data or key material may transit outside the US.

I attached our draft DPA (DPA_GreenStreet_v1.pdf) and an SOW template. Can you confirm the expected responses/timeline? Ideally we’d have redlines back within a week so procurement can include the vendor in the Q3 list.

Thanks,

Sarah
Sarah Lowe
Head of Procurement
GreenStreet Health

-- Attachment: SOW_GreenStreet_2027.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 120KB)
From: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
To: Sarah Lowe <sarah.lowe@greenstreethealth.com>, Alan Yeung <alan.yeung@greenstreethealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 2 May 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GreenStreet — private deploy DPA + keystore questions

Sarah — thanks for the clear list, and great to hear the demo was helpful. High level answers below; we’ll follow up with a short redline and a technical appendix.

1) BYOK / customer CMK: Yes — our private deployment supports a customer-controlled keystore (BYOK) where the customer provides and manages the CMK in their KMS. Redwood’s control plane is configured to never possess plaintext keys for customer data in BYOK mode. We can add DPA language that specifies that Redwood does not have the ability to decrypt customer payloads when BYOK is enabled, and we can include a keystore-handshake checklist in the SOW.

2) Operator access & telemetry: For private deployments we minimize control-plane telemetry to operational metrics and anonymized routing telemetry. We keep operator console access gated (RBAC + MFA) and require break-glass approval workflows for any emergency access. Retention for operational logs is configurable; default is 30 days, can be shortened to 7 days for higher security customers. We will provide sample telemetry extracts for audit.

3) Subprocessors: For private deployments hosted in customer VPC/on-prem, the list of subprocessors is narrower — primarily our support bundle processing (s3-equivalent archived artifacts) and a regional infra partner for hardware support. We will provide a subprocessors list and agree to 30 days’ notice for non-emergency additions.

4) Cross-border transfers: In BYOK private mode we avoid any customer data egress from the customer VPC unless explicitly routed for support/escrow operations; we can commit to a US-only routing config for your account. If operator-assisted key escrow is required, we will document where key escrow artifacts are stored and require explicit customer consent for cross-border storage.

I’m cc’ing Ben (sales lead) and Laura (privacy/ops) to align on contract language and technical appendix. We’ll prepare a redline of the DPA and a one-page keystore appendix by EOD Wednesday.

Best,

Markus Klein
VP, Solutions & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — quick procurement note from our side:

- We can sign the DPA redline you proposed but suggest a short SOW addendum for the keystore onboarding steps and a fixed engineer-hours estimate for any on-site validation (if required).
- Pricing: by default BYOK private deployments carry an operator-minimization discount (since we’re not hosting keys), I’ll include a pricing note in the SOW addendum.

If helpful, I can loop in our procurement manager to take the DocuSign flow once legal confirms redlines. Proposed timeline: Redwood sends redline Wed EOD, GreenStreet redline back Fri, DocuSign next week.

Cheers,

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: Sarah Lowe <sarah.lowe@greenstreethealth.com>, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
Cc: dpa-legal@heronlaw.com
Date: Wed, 4 May 2027 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GreenStreet — private deploy DPA + keystore questions

Hi all — adding a short technical appendix here for what we will include with the redline. Feel free to forward to your security reviewers.

- Keystore handshake: documented steps for CMK provisioning (customer KMS IAM role, attestation challenge, ephemeral session tokens). We will not import or mirror customer CMKs into Redwood-managed KMS in BYOK mode.
- Operator access model: operator-only roles are split from control plane administrators. Emergency access requires a three-party approval (customer SEA, Redwood on-call, and on-call manager) and is logged to an immutable audit trail.
- Telemetry & logs: control-plane metrics + system health (CPU/mem/gpu) — no user payloads. Support bundles are redacted for PII and kept in customer-owned storage when requested.
- Evidence package: 1) sample telemetry extract, 2) operator access audit snippet, 3) subprocessors list and contact details.

Attached is a small telemetry sample and a checklist we use for keystore onboarding. If your security team wants an on-site (or captive VPC) review, we can schedule a 2-4 hour technical validation session.

Regards,

Laura Bennett
Senior Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Alan Yeung <alan.yeung@greenstreethealth.com>

Date: Thu, 5 May 2027 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GreenStreet — private deploy DPA + keystore questions

Thanks — team liked the quick summary. Our counsel reviewed and had two asks before we escalate to procurement:

1) We need explicit DPA wording that states Redwood will not have means to decrypt customer data when BYOK is enabled, plus a short protocol describing how Redwood will demonstrate this (attestation steps and sample audit snippets).
2) Subprocessor notice period: counsel wants 45 days for non-emergency subprocessors instead of 30. Emergency additions may remain immediate with post-notice.

We’ve attached a version of your DPA with inline comments (coming from DPA Counsel). Can you confirm you’ll accept the attestation protocol language and the 45-day notice for non-emergency subprocessors? If yes, procurement will prepare the purchase order and DocuSign package.

Alan Yeung
Director, Vendor Operations
GreenStreet Health

-- Attachment: DPA_GreenStreet_v1_redlines_from_counsel.pdf (application/pdf, 110KB)
From: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
To: Alan Yeung <alan.yeung@greenstreethealth.com>, Sarah Lowe <sarah.lowe@greenstreethealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, dpa-legal@heronlaw.com
Date: Fri, 6 May 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GreenStreet — private deploy DPA + keystore questions

Alan/Sarah — appreciate the clear asks. Short answers: yes on both, with small clarifications.

- Attestation protocol: we will add a short attestation appendix to the DPA describing the keystore handshake and sample audit outputs (signed verification of the KMS policy, ephemeral session log sample, and audit hashes). We will accept language stating Redwood does not have the ability to decrypt customer data in BYOK mode. The attestation appendix will be part of the SOW.
- Subprocessor notice: we can accept 45 days’ notice for non-emergency subprocessors. For emergency infrastructure support (hardware replacement, critical security fix) we will provide immediate notice and remedial details within 7 days.

Next steps: Redwood legal will send an updated DPA redline (with attestation appendix) by end of day Monday. Ben — please prepare the SOW addendum and the DocuSign flow once legal confirms. Sarah/Alan — appreciate the timeline confirmation; we’ll aim to have DocuSign ready early next week.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this across the finish line.

Best,

Markus Klein
VP, Solutions & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
